14.0.s.en: 1. The personal iniquity of the enquirer:

14.0.0.en: 1 Then came certain of the elders of Israel unto me, and sat before me. 2 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 3 "Son of man, these men have set up their idols in their heart, and put the stumblingblock of their iniquity before their face: should I be enquired of at all by them? 4 Therefore speak unto them, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Every man of the house of Israel that setteth up his idols in his heart, and putteth the stumblingblock of his iniquity before his face, and cometh to the prophet; I the LORD will answer him that cometh according to the multitude of his idols; 5 That I may take the house of Israel in their own heart, because they are all estranged from me through their idols. 6 Therefore say unto the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Repent, and turn yourselves from your idols; and turn away your faces from all your abominations. 7 For every one of the house of Israel, or of the stranger that sojourneth in Israel, which separateth himself from me, and setteth up his idols in his heart, and putteth the stumblingblock of his iniquity before his face, and cometh to a prophet to enquire of him concerning me; I the LORD will answer him by myself: 8 And I will set my face against that man, and will make him a sign and a proverb, and I will cut him off from the midst of my people; and ye shall know that I am the LORD."

14.1.0.en: When men from the elders of Israel came and sat before him to enquire, the word of the Lord came to him: "Son of man, these men have set up their idols in their heart, and put the stumblingblock of their iniquity before their face: should I be enquired of at all by them?" [3]. Truly they came to ask God, not the idols, asking Him through Ezekiel himself, the true prophet. But how can God answer the question of one who has worshipped idols in his heart? Their unseen iniquity became a stumblingblock that shut the door of God's answer in their faces. He answers not according to the heart of the prophet but according to the multitude of their idols, which have taken possession of their hearts [4-5].

14.2.0.en: He withheld His answer from them in order to stir up in them the spirit of repentance... "Repent, and turn yourselves from your idols; and turn away your faces from all your abominations" [6]. He speaks to them with complete frankness: He will not answer them until they drive their idols out of their hearts, so that the Lord Himself may again reign in the heart.

14.3.s.en: 2. The personal iniquity of the prophet:

14.3.0.en: 9 And if the prophet be deceived when he hath spoken a thing, I the LORD have deceived that prophet, and I will stretch out my hand upon him, and will destroy him from the midst of my people Israel. 10 And they shall bear the punishment of their iniquity: the punishment of the prophet shall be even as the punishment of him that seeketh unto him; 11 That the house of Israel may go no more astray from me, neither be polluted any more with all their transgressions; but that they may be my people, and I may be their God, saith the Lord GOD."

14.3.1.en: "And if the prophet be deceived when he hath spoken a thing, I the LORD have deceived that prophet, and I will stretch out my hand upon him, and will destroy him from the midst of my people Israel. And they shall bear the punishment of their iniquity: the punishment of the prophet shall be even as the punishment of him that seeketh unto him" [9-10]. I show no partiality: if the enquirer sins, I repay him according to his wicked heart, and if the prophet sins, I repay him according to his heart. God judges the priest as He judges the people, the servant as those he serves.

14.4.s.en: 3. Man's accountability for his own conduct:

14.4.0.en: 12 The word of the LORD came again to me, saying, 13 "Son of man, when the land sinneth against me by trespassing grievously, then will I stretch out mine hand upon it, and will break the staff of the bread thereof, and will send famine upon it, and will cut off man and beast from it: 14 Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness, saith the Lord GOD. 15 If I cause noisome beasts to pass through the land, and they spoil it, so that it be desolate, that no man may pass through because of the beasts: 16 Though these three men were in it, as I live, saith the Lord GOD, they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters; they only shall be delivered, but the land shall be desolate. 17 Or if I bring a sword upon that land, and say, Sword, go through the land; so that I cut off man and beast from it: 18 Though these three men were in it, as I live, saith the Lord GOD, they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters, but they only shall be delivered themselves. 19 Or if I send a pestilence into that land, and pour out my fury upon it in blood, to cut off from it man and beast: 20 Though Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, as I live, saith the Lord GOD, they shall deliver neither son nor daughter; they shall but deliver their own souls by their righteousness."

14.5.0.en: The word of God came to him: "Son of man, when the land sinneth against me by trespassing grievously, then will I stretch out mine hand upon it, and will break the staff of the bread thereof, and will send famine upon it, and will cut off man and beast from it: though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness, saith the Lord GOD" [13-14].

14.5.1.en: He says, "when the land sinneth against me"; what does he mean by the land?

14.5.2.en: a. Origen sees that it does not mean the inhabitants of the land.

14.5.3.en: b. In his view every sinner is counted as earth: [The sinner is called earth, because it was said to Adam: "Thou art earth, and unto earth shalt thou return" (Gen 3:19). Thus we can say that the commission of sin makes the sinner earth... When the earth beholds God, it trembles and is troubled... and we also, like the earth, tremble and are troubled because of our sins].

14.5.4.en: The Lord affirmed that if the land sinned and betrayed Him, and He struck it with famine, and these three, "Noah, Daniel, and Job," were in it, they would not deliver anyone, but their own souls would be delivered by their righteousness. Then He affirmed again that if the land were struck with noisome, ravening beasts which bereaved its inhabitants, these men would deliver neither sons nor daughters. A third time, if the Lord brought a sword to cut off man and beast from the land, these three would not deliver sons or daughters. And finally, a fourth time, if He brought a pestilence upon the land and poured out His fury upon it in blood, these would deliver neither son nor daughter, but would deliver their own souls by their righteousness. It is as though the Lord, in the Book of Ezekiel, were constantly affirming man's personal responsibility for his faith and his life: we have seen the enquirer (the people) bearing his own iniquity, and the prophet also, and here He affirms that if He finds a righteous man, that man is saved, but he cannot rescue even his son or daughter if the children do not walk in righteousness like their fathers. If this generation is of the seed of Abraham, the father of the fathers and the man of faith, that profits them nothing; and if the generation before them turned aside to idol worship, that does not bind them to the divine wrath, but they are called to account for themselves... This is what He will affirm again, more clearly, in chapter eighteen.

14.5.5.en: In the light of this chapter we understand the role of the saints in our life, as St. John Chrysostom says: [If we are negligent, we cannot obtain our salvation, not even by the help of others... I say this not to set aside the petitions of the saints, but to put an end to your negligence and to your contentment with relying on others while you lie flat on your backs], and he also says: [How great are the blessings of the prayers of the saints, if we also are working].

14.5.6.en: Intercession for the people was a living part of the work of the prophets and priests. The prophet Samuel says: "Moreover as for me, God forbid that I should sin against the LORD in ceasing to pray for you" (1 Sam 12:23). And at Mizpeh, when the Philistines rose up against them, they said to Samuel: "Cease not to cry unto the LORD our God for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines" (1 Sam 7:8). Moses also interceded for his people, until the Lord said to him: "Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation" (Ex 32:10)... The prayers of the saints support the striving soul that desires repentance, but if it persists in its stubbornness they avail it nothing, for the Lord says to the prophet Jeremiah: "Therefore pray not thou for this people, neither lift up cry nor prayer for them, neither make intercession to me: for I will not hear thee" (Jer 7:16; 11:14). God, who said, "For I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David's sake" (2 Kgs 19:14), in the days of Hezekiah the righteous king, did not say this in the days of abounding evil, when He delivered the city to Nebuchadnezzar.

14.6.s.en: Why did He choose these men: Noah, Daniel and Job?

14.6.0.en: Perhaps because they represent a sample of righteous men who lived in the midst of the wicked: Noah lived among a corrupt generation that deserved the flood, and Job kept his righteousness in a pagan environment. As for Daniel, either the Daniel who lived with the three young men in the land of captivity, pure, far from every possibility of a holy life, is meant, or perhaps the Daniel mentioned in the tablets of Ras-shamra, which go back to about 1400 B.C., a wise man and a Phoenician judge, who judged justly in the cases of widows and orphans. In this way the Lord rebuked this Jewish people, for He presented three righteous men who were not Hebrews: Noah and Job, who lived before Abraham, and Daniel, a Phoenician man, as though God were affirming to them that He shows no partiality. He desires the salvation of every soul, whatever its race, as long as it responds to His love and His commandment.

14.6.1.en: St. Augustine sees that these men represent types, for he says: [In these three men God undoubtedly presented types of the three ranks of men who are saved].

14.6.2.en: I believe that Noah represents the righteous leaders of the nations, because of his ordering of the flood as a type of the Church, Daniel represents the righteous in purity, and Job represents the righteous who are married.

14.6.3.en: Origen sees that each of the three passed through three stages: a period of happiness followed by a stage of sorrow and pain, then a return to joy and happiness. Thus a man begins his spiritual life with divine consolations, followed by a narrow way and troubles that bring him into new spiritual glories... This is the way of the glorified Cross, or the way of fellowship with the suffering Christ who rose from the dead, or the way of salvation.

14.6.4.en: The bitter punishments under which man falls because of his sins are four:

14.6.5.en: a. Famine, which cuts off man and beast from the land [13].

14.7.0.en: b. Noisome beasts, which turn the land into a desolation and bereave mothers [15].

14.8.0.en: c. The sword, which cuts off man and beast from the land [17].

14.9.0.en: d. The pestilence, which pours out God's fury upon the land in blood [19].

14.9.1.en: As for His mention of "man and beast," it is because man points to the rational or soul side, and the beast to the bodily side; as though sin, which deprives man of God, causes him to lose both the spiritual and the temporal blessings, or the blessings of the inner soul and also of the body.

14.9.2.en: Hunger, the loss of security (the noisome beasts), the removal of peace (the sword), and the deprivation of health (the pestilence) are the natural fruits that man gathers from sin, which isolates him from God, the source of his satisfaction, security, peace and health. Therefore, when St. Augustine feels hunger and anxiety he takes refuge in God, addressing Him:

14.9.3.en: [My God... You have made my soul able to contain Your infinite majesty, lest it have anything that is able to fill it besides You!

14.9.4.en: My God... You have made us for Yourself... therefore our heart remains troubled, anxious, and without rest at all times until it rests in You].

14.9.5.en: These strokes, with the types they carry, represent four aspects resulting from the work of sin in man's life: famine, because of the loss of the knowledge of the truth; the noisome beasts, which represent the domination of the demons over the soul, so that they kill every virtue in it and make the soul like a bereaved mother without hope; the sword, in that man loses his vitality and becomes like one slain, of no use; and finally the pestilence, in that man becomes a germ of corruption that destroys those around him. It is as though the strokes signify man's deprivation of the truth and his subjection to the domination of the devil, his deprivation of all vitality and his becoming a focus of corruption for others!

14.10.s.en: 4. God's care for the repentant remnant:

14.10.0.en: 21 "For thus saith the Lord GOD; How much more when I send my four sore judgments upon Jerusalem, the sword, and the famine, and the noisome beast, and the pestilence, to cut off from it man and beast? 22 Yet, behold, therein shall be left a remnant that shall be brought forth, both sons and daughters: behold, they shall come forth unto you, and ye shall see their way and their doings: and ye shall be comforted concerning the evil that I have brought upon Jerusalem, even concerning all that I have brought upon it. 23 And they shall comfort you, when ye see their ways and their doings: and ye shall know that I have not done without cause all that I have done in it, saith the Lord GOD."

14.10.1.en: Every time God speaks of the chastening of His people or of His wrath because of their multiplied sins, He does not forget to affirm His care for the small repentant remnant.

14.10.2.en: I have sinned! I have sinned!

14.10.3.en: * My God... how hard it is for my soul to confess!

14.10.4.en: Reveal to me my hidden depths, that I may cry out:

14.10.5.en: I have sinned! I have sinned!

14.10.6.en: * In former times the people laid the blame on the priests, and the priests laid the blame on the people, and every generation thought that it was being punished for the faults of its fathers.

14.10.8.en: I have sinned! I have sinned!

14.10.9.en: * My father will not intercede for me if I neglect my salvation!

14.10.10.en: And I will not be punished for his weaknesses!

14.10.11.en: I confess to You my personal responsibility!

14.10.12.en: I have sinned, so pardon me and forgive me!

14.10.13.en: * The prophet Moses interceded for his people, and the prophet Samuel did not cease to pray for them; we are surrounded by a cloud of witnesses, who intercede and pray for us and support us!

14.10.14.en: Teach me to care for the salvation of my soul, so that the cloud may truly be a support to me!

14.10.15.en: * I complain to You of my soul, for sin has shattered me:

14.10.16.en: A famine of the word of the Lord has come upon me!

14.10.17.en: I have become a wilderness, in which evil thoughts dwell like noisome beasts!

14.10.18.en: The sword of sin has struck my depths, shattering my powers!

14.10.19.en: By my sin I have become like a corrupting pestilence to those around me.

14.10.20.en: I confess my sin to You, for I alone am the debtor!

15.0.0.en: 1 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 "Son of man, What is the vine tree more than any tree, or than a branch which is among the trees of the forest? 3 Shall wood be taken thereof to do any work? or will men take a pin of it to hang any vessel thereon? 4 Behold, it is cast into the fire for fuel; the fire devoureth both the ends of it, and the midst of it is burned. Is it meet for any work? 5 Behold, when it was whole, it was meet for no work: how much less shall it be meet yet for any work, when the fire hath devoured it, and it is burned? 6 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; As the vine tree among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so will I give the inhabitants of Jerusalem. 7 And I will set my face against them; they shall go out from one fire, and another fire shall devour them; and ye shall know that I am the LORD, when I set my face against them. 8 And I will make the land desolate, because they have committed a trespass, saith the Lord GOD."

15.0.1.en: God often addresses His people as His divine vineyard, which He planted with His right hand and tended Himself, and which He never left in want of anything. God chose the vine because among the other trees it is considered small, with pliant wood... its wood is not fit as planks for building purposes, nor as cords and supports for tents, nor even as fuel, for the fire devours it entirely in moments... Almost its only distinction is its abundant fruit. If it does not bear fruit, it is good for nothing at all. So it is with what God requires of His Church: the precious fruit of the Spirit.

15.0.2.en: In the prophet Isaiah He declares that He set it on a fruitful hill, He fenced it and gathered out the stones thereof, and built a tower in the midst of it, and also made a winepress therein (Isa 5:1-2). He gave it every possibility of bearing fruit: He hedged it about with His Holy Spirit, took away from it the stony nature, and gave it the tower of divine knowledge... and He looked for good fruit, and behold, it brought forth wild grapes. Therefore He punishes it, saying: "And now, O inhabitants of Jerusalem, and men of Judah, judge, I pray you, betwixt me and my vineyard. What could have been done more to my vineyard, that I have not done in it? wherefore, when I looked that it should bring forth grapes, brought it forth wild grapes? And now go to; I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up; and break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down: And I will lay it waste: it shall not be pruned, nor digged; but there shall come up briers and thorns: I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it. For the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant: and he looked for judgment, but behold bloodshed; for righteousness, but behold a cry" (Isa 5:3-7).

15.0.3.en: Again the Psalmist describes the people of God as the vine of the Lord, which He tended with His right hand, but which did not keep its being... for he says: "Thou hast brought a vine out of Egypt: thou hast cast out the heathen, and planted it. Thou preparedst room before it, and didst cause it to take deep root, and it filled the land. The hills were covered with the shadow of it, and the boughs thereof were like the goodly cedars. She sent out her boughs unto the sea, and her branches unto the river. Why hast thou then broken down her hedges, so that all they which pass by the way do pluck her? The boar out of the wood doth waste it, and the wild beast of the field doth devour it" (Ps 80:8-13).

15.0.4.en: This is what happened literally to the people of Israel, as it happens symbolically in the life of many. Literally, the Lord established His people in Egypt as the first plant, on the level of a nation of His own, then transplanted it from there by the hand of Moses, with a high hand and a strong arm. He drove out many nations from before its face that it might dwell in the Promised Land, so its people multiplied and increased in number and filled the Promised Land, and embraced the mountains of Israel and the cedars of Lebanon, extending east of the Mediterranean to the river Jordan... But when it turned away from God, the Lord broke down its wall, and many strangers entered it and humbled it, and it became unclean by the entry of idolatrous worship into its temple, and instead of the Lord's care for it, the wild beast within it came to devour its children.

15.0.5.en: Symbolically, however, the believer, planted in Egypt (the world), is brought by the Lord across to the heavenly Jerusalem, and is led into the heavenly places by the hand of the Lord Christ Himself with a strong hand. He drives out from before him all the powers of darkness, so that they have no place in his heart, and he lives as a king, having authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, embracing within himself the holy mountains (the prophets of the Old Testament and the apostles of the New Testament) and the cedars of God, as he enters into fellowship with the saints who live in the uprightness of the cedar. His life extends to the sea and the river, that is, to the streams of holy waters, or the blessed river of Baptism, that it may live by the Holy Spirit of God as the secret of its enlightenment and its constant growth. Such a soul, if it does not stand firm in what has been given it to the end, is lost and becomes the plaything of Satan! Therefore the Apostle Paul warns us: "Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall" (1 Cor 10:12).

15.1.0.en: If the Church of the Old Testament, like that of the New Testament, was called a vine among the trees of the forest, because it bore the cluster of life, the Lord of glory Jesus, who is the secret of our joy and exultation, and bore fruit among the unfruitful trees of the forest, then in this chapter the ancient people is called the vine tree more than any tree, or than the branch which is among the trees of the forest. It is the branch of the vine which was required to bear the cluster, but alas, being cut off from the root, it became dry and useless. It dried up, and the fire devoured both its ends and burned its midst; is it meet for any work? "Behold, when it was whole, it was meet for no work: how much less shall it be meet yet for any work, when the fire hath devoured it, and it is burned?" [5].

15.1.1.en: First: it was cut off from the root, so it lost its life and was no longer fit for anything but to be burned with the fire of judgment, and as St. Augustine says: [The branch suits only one of two things: either the vine or the fire. If it does not abide in the vine, its portion is the fire. And if it wishes to escape the latter place, it must have its place in the vine].

15.1.2.en: Second: the burning of its two ends is a reference to what befell this people because of their sins, for the northern kingdom fell in 721 B.C. in the Assyrian captivity, and the southern kingdom in its first captivity, about 597 B.C. What befell it, its withdrawal from God Himself, was an inner burning because of sin. Therefore the total burning must needs come.

15.1.3.en: Make me abide in You, O true Vine!

15.1.4.en: * Make me abide in You, O true Vine, for without You I wither and am not fit even for the burning!

15.1.5.en: * Behold, I am a bruised reed; do not break me!

15.1.6.en: Mend my state with the touches of Your healing hand!

15.1.7.en: Grant me Your Holy Spirit working in me!

15.1.8.en: Instead of dryness let me bear living fruits, and instead of death let me breathe eternal life!

15.1.9.en: * You watered Your vineyard with Your precious blood; You planted Your Church as a good vine, You surrounded it with the walls of Your Holy Spirit, and You gave it every possibility of bearing fruit!

15.1.10.en: Work, that I may bear Your fruit within me, O Holy One!
